analytics.name: Analytic 1869
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) host or server establishing outbound connections on a commonly-allowed port (e.g., 443, 80, 8080, 53, etc.) to a destination not in the approved vendor/business domain list, where that host's documented network role does not require external connectivity. Documented real-world use: Sandworm's 2015 Ukraine power grid attack used port 443 for Command and Control (C2) communications. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity. SNI and certificate attributes are TLS/session metadata; do not treat them as decrypted payload content. Encrypted application content requires a separate inspection point.

tuning.description: Allowlist of legitimate vendor domains for software updates, licensing, or remote support.
Inventory of ICS hosts whose documented function never requires outbound internet connectivity.
